items.content_html:
Description

Update PR checks to run through one aggregate workflow.

  • Convert the individual check workflows into reusable workflows.
  • Select checks by changed files and report a single aggregate result.
  • Move the concurrency group to the aggregate workflow, so a new push cancels the whole run.

Motivation

Allow one required status check while keeping individual checks selective.

Additional details

The branch protection ruleset must switch the required status check from Check Redirects / check-redirects to PR checks / all-checks-passed-or-skipped when this merges. Otherwise the old required check stays pending forever and blocks merges.

Check names in the PR UI change to PR checks / <check> / <job> (e.g. PR checks / lint_content / lint).

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: ci(pr-checks): add aggregate reusable checks

items.content_html:
Description

Clarify that normal CSS injected with tabs.insertCSS({ cssOrigin: "user" }) does not override website author styles, while user-origin declarations marked !important do.

Motivation

The current wording suggests that selecting "user" alone prevents websites from overriding injected CSS. This can mislead extension authors who omit !important.

Additional details

The CSS Cascade Level 5 specification ranks normal author declarations above normal user declarations, and important user declarations above important author declarations.

Documentation-only change. Verified with git diff --check.

Related issues and pull requests

Relates to #43033.
items.title: docs: clarify user-origin CSS priority in tabs.insertCSS

items.content_html:
Bumps the npm-dev group with 1 update: cspell.

Updates cspell from 10.3.4 to 10.3.5

Release notes

Sourced from cspell's releases.

v10.3.5

Fixes

fix(cspell-lib): shouldCheckDocument honors the forceCheck option (#9303)

Summary

For users of the cspell-lib API:

  • shouldCheckDocument now honors forceCheck. It returns shouldCheck: true for a document excluded by ignorePaths, or disabled by overrides or languageSettings. Before, the option was accepted but ignored. DocumentValidator already worked this way.
  • SpellCheckFileOptions now declares forceCheck, so it can be passed to spellCheckDocument and spellCheckFile with type checking.

fix: --force-check checks the listed files even when ignorePaths or files would skip them (#9300)

Summary

--force-check now checks every file given with --file or --file-list, as its help says. Before, some of those files were still skipped:

  • files matched by ignorePaths in the config;
  • files that don't match the files setting in the config.

Using globs on the command line together with --force-check is now an error, the same as globs with --file:

error: mixing globs and --force-check is not supported

Before, cspell lint --file-list list.txt "**/*.md" --force-check was accepted. To filter a file list by glob, leave out --force-check.

fix: files globs starting with ** no longer skip --file and --file-list files in a project under a dot folder (#9299)

Summary

When a project was under a folder whose name starts with a dot, such as ~/.local/src/my-project or a git worktree in .claude/worktrees/, files given with --file or --file-list could be skipped without any warning. CSpell then reported Files checked: 0 and exited with success.

Description

Adds two things to IDBFactory.deleteDatabase():

  • A paragraph on what happens while a deletion is blocked: open connections keep working until they are closed, and later open() / deleteDatabase() requests for the same database wait behind the pending deletion.
  • A "Handling a blocked deletion" example that listens for blocked alongside success.

Motivation

#44350 already explains why a deletion gets blocked and how to unblock it. Readers still had to work out on their own what the blocked state means for existing connections and for new requests (points 3 and 4 of the issue), and the page had no example that handles blocked.

Additional details

IndexedDB spec: deleting a database and opening a database both add the request to the connection queue for the storage key and name, and wait for earlier requests in that queue. Firefox report that prompted the issue: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2006245

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #42779
Relates to #44350
items.title: IDBFactory.deleteDatabase(): explain what happens while a deletion is blocked

items.content_html:
Description

This PR corrects several technical claims on the ARIA document role page.

Motivation

  • The example placed a document inside a dialog and called the dialog a composite widget. dialog is a window role, and the spec says the document role only changes assistive technology behavior inside a widget or application. The example now uses application, which matches the spec's own example, and a short note explains why a dialog doesn't need the role.
  • aria-expanded is not a supported state on the document role, so I removed it from the attribute list and from "Required JavaScript features".
  • tabindex is an HTML attribute, so I removed it from the ARIA attribute list. The keyboard interactions section now links to it instead.
  • Best practices now mentions that tabindex="0" adds the element to the tab order, and that widgets using arrow-key focus management need to let users reach the document content and get back to the widget.
  • The comparison with article said document elements have no relation to each other. The spec doesn't say this, and the issue points out it could mislead authors, so I removed the paragraph.

Additional details

  • Spec: document role (supported states do not include aria-expanded) and window roles.
  • markdownlint-cli2 and prettier --check on the page report 0 issues, and the front-matter linter passes.
  • Previewed with npm start: the page renders with no flaws, and the new roving tabindex anchor resolves.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #33746
items.title: Fix technical claims on the ARIA document role page
